avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, control of emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: The city buys trees and has them planted on public land, and it pays an organization to green private and institutional land. Boroughs add their own means: money from park funds, machinery rental, blue-collar crews. Exemptions also apply to tree planting in two building projects.

etapes.texte: City council awards contracts to 7574479 Canada inc. and to Terrassement Technique Sylvain Labrecque inc. to supply and plant 1,374 trees, then water, maintain and replace some of them. The maximum expense is $2,456,590.55, taxes included, for trees spread across seven boroughs.

Pierrefonds-Roxboro transfers up to $162,233.12 from its fund reserved for parks purposes to the purchase of trees and plants. City council pays $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional sites from March 24 to December 31, 2026.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an extension at 1620, rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening instead of the required 40 trees and 25%. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger, for a two-storey building.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini backhoe loader with operator for $152,916.75, taxes included, and sets aside $200,000 for additional blue-collar crews assigned to planting, from May to November 2026. Outremont entrusts URBEX Construction inc. with the renovation of the parc Pratt chalet and the redevelopment of its surroundings, including planting of vegetation, partly financed by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

City council leases land in the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for a total rent of $100 before taxes. The organization stores materials, equipment and trees intended for planting there.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit its accountability report by December 31, 2026, at the latest, then its report and financial statements by March 31, 2027.
The lease for the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood nursery runs until April 30, 2028.

deneigement.description: Snow removal and loading contracts, spreading of abrasives, parking by-laws.

etapes.titre: Spring cleaning of streets and sidewalks
etapes.texte: Several boroughs are renting vacuum sweepers, tanker trucks, sidewalk washers and a mini sweeper with operators to remove abrasives after winter. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is authorizing an expenditure of $574,920.99, taxes included, for four vacuum sweepers and three tanker trucks in 2026 and 2027.

etapes.titre: Snow removal from downtown public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie is contracting companies to maintain, clean and remove snow from Square Viger, Place des Montréalaises, square Dorchester, place du Canada, îlot Bonaventure, square Victoria, place du Sable-Gris and square Chaboillez. The borough is also extending snow removal in the Quartier des Spectacles by one year, from April 2, 2026 to April 1, 2027.

Montréal-Nord is paying for an additional rented grader during the 2025-2026 winter, and Saint-Léonard is allocating $200,000 in surplus to its 2026 snow removal operations, after 39 abrasive spreadings since November 15, 2025, while the budget had planned for 20. The City and some boroughs are extending turnkey snow removal, towing, and equipment rental with operators contracts by 12 months.

etapes.titre: Snow removal for parks and buildings
etapes.texte: The City is extending snow removal for the parking lot of the édifice Jacinthe-Fyfe and for parc Frédéric-Back, the TAZ and the stade de soccer de Montréal. It is also awarding a contract to remove snow from service roads and parking lots in the Grand parc de l'Ouest, in the Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche and Cap-Saint-Jacques sectors.

aSurveiller.texte: Snow removal services for the Grand parc de l'Ouest cover two seasons, from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
The extended towing contracts begin on November 15, 2026.
The turnkey snow removal contract for Le Plateau-Mont-Royal ends on April 15, 2031, with each season running from November 1 to April 15.
The turnkey snow removal contracts for Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Lachine, Outremont and Le Sud-Ouest end on April 15, 2030.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: This year, the City is funding and launching work on its drinking water and sewer networks, in several boroughs and on main pipes. It is also continuing the wastewater disinfection project at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant and paying for the plant's ongoing operation. Boroughs are taking charge of replacing lead water service lines, including the portion located on private property.

etapes.texte: The City is awarding contracts to rehabilitate secondary water pipes by lining, without trench digging, and to redo the roadway in various streets in many boroughs. These contracts include the replacement of lead water service lines on both the public and private side.

etapes.titre: Lead water service lines on private property
etapes.texte: Boroughs are offering city council the option to take charge of replacing lead service lines located on private property, under by-law 20-030. The costs of work done on private property are billed to the property owners concerned [CA26 22 0034].

The City is awarding contracts to rebuild water pipes and infrastructure along rue Guy and on rue De Champlain, and is adding funds to the contracts for rue Saint-Antoine Ouest and rue de la Cathédrale. On rue De Champlain, the work replaces a 1,200 mm pipe installed in 1927 [CG26 0332].

The City is renewing or awarding contracts to operate the wastewater treatment plant: process control system, chemicals, residue landfilling, housekeeping, upgrading of the sludge incinerators and mechanical work. The mechanical work aims in particular to recondition screens damaged during heavy rains [CG26 0543].

aSurveiller.texte: Shutdown of sludge incinerator 2 in the first week of October 2026, then incinerator 4 in January 2027, for about six weeks of work each.
Adoption expected on October 19, 2026 of the $951,000,000 loan by-law for the renewal of secondary waterworks and sewer networks.
Rehabilitation work on the 600 mm pipe along autoroute 15 Nord to be completed by December 18, 2026 at the latest.
Completion of the rue de la Cathédrale pipe work pushed back from December 2026 to March 2027.
Rue Guy worksite planned until December 2027; commissioning of the ozone plant planned for 2029.

frederic-back.titre: Frédéric-Back Park and Saint-Michel Environmental Complex
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned dump, transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, electrical system upgrades.
frederic-back.enBref: This year, the City is moving forward with several projects at Frédéric-Back park and the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel. It is launching the construction of a greenhouse complex in the Saint-Michel neighbourhood, replacing electrical equipment at the site, renewing park maintenance, and redeveloping rue De Louvain around the park. It is also asking the Quebec government for money for a cycling and pedestrian link.

etapes.texte: The City is asking the Quebec ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable for financial help to build a footbridge and an east-west link in the park. The file describes a 900-metre trail crossing the park, including a footbridge of about 150 metres, and funding of up to $2,000,000 [CG26 0121].

The City approves the construction of a greenhouse complex near the composting platform, then hands the project to the Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough. The borough then awards a contract of $499,865.92, taxes included, to supply and install two greenhouses, with $74,979.88 in contingencies [CA26 14 0163].

The City awards a contract of $1,091,693.37, taxes included, for the second phase of electrical work at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel, with $163,754.01 in contingencies. The work covers a new 25 kV power supply, a transformer, a backup generator, and a controller to manage biogas capture [CG26 0223].

The borough awards a contract of up to $8,199,514.82, taxes included, to redevelop rue De Louvain between Frédéric-Back park and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a total authorized expense of $11,192,464.62. The work covers sewers, water mains, lighting, sidewalks, the bike path, and plantings [CA26 14 0076].

The City hands two companies the general upkeep and ecological and horticultural management of the park for 30 months, from May 1, 2026 to October 31, 2028. It is also extending by six months the snow removal contract for the park, the TAZ, and the soccer stadium, for $193,215.49 more, taxes included [CG26 0521].

The City is extending by five months the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor with operator at the complex, for $296,349.21 more, taxes included; the compost is used in part to landscape the park [CG26 0320]. In October, the borough authorizes filing a funding request to the Véloce III program for the bike lane and sidewalks on rue De Louvain Est.

aSurveiller.texte: The call for projects under the TAPU program, for which the City is filing its request, ends on November 26, 2026.
The greenhouse installation work is to be completed in December 2026; the greenhouses are announced to open in winter 2027.
The extended snow removal contract covers November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027.
Work on rue De Louvain continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, bump-outs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).
26 more hectares will be added to the park in 2027, in the Boisé Ouest sector.

grand-parc-ouest.description: The largest municipal park in Canada, being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.

etapes.titre: More money for the heritage walls
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98, taxes included, to the contract for repairing the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77, taxes included. The file explains the costs by unforeseen site conditions: buried stones that had to be cleaned by hand, extra mortar, sod, and a deteriorated culvert that needs replacing.

The City is submitting the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques area (330 hectares) for the international Urban Night Sky Place designation from DarkSky International. Filing the application does not commit any spending; if the designation is granted, the City commits to producing a lighting plan, bringing its light fixtures up to standard, and keeping the site accessible at night.

etapes.titre: Two areas listed as natural environments
etapes.texte: The parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector of the Grand parc de l'Ouest (429 ha) are added to the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité (directory of natural environments protected and contributing to biodiversity) of the agglomeration, with conservation plans. The 2025 report filed shows 4,051 ha listed or provisionally listed, or 8.1% of the agglomeration's territory.

A contract of $366,117.31, taxes included, goes to Gendron Gestion Civil inc. to rebuild the culvert under chemin Senneville, as part of modernizing the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub; total spending reaches $481,850.45, taxes included. The undersized culvert had been damaged by the heavy rains of August 2024.

etapes.titre: Snow clearing, cleaning and tree felling
etapes.texte: The City is awarding Paysagiste Solarco inc. the snow clearing of service roads and parking lots in the Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche and Cap-Saint-Jacques areas ($178,330.82, taxes included), and 9232-3914 Québec inc. the housekeeping of nine Cap-Saint-Jacques buildings ($704,619.24, taxes included). Entrepreneur Paysagiste Strathmore (1997) ltée will fell ash trees and other dying trees in the park, for a total expense of $1,713,041.27, taxes included.

aSurveiller.texte: Snow clearing of service roads and parking lots from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
Housekeeping of nine Cap-Saint-Jacques buildings from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2030, with a possible extension until October 31, 2031.
Felling of ash trees and dying trees from fall 2026 to early summer 2028.
Cap-Saint-Jacques lighting management plan filed in February 2027, response from DarkSky International expected in April 2027, full site compliance by April 2032.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warming centres and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: The City lends municipal buildings to organizations to open warming centres, and it funds organizations that work with people experiencing homelessness. It also deploys a Ville-Marie public works team to other boroughs for cleanliness interventions related to homelessness. It is putting in place a framework to receive private donations and is appealing a ruling on encampments under the Van Horne viaduct.

etapes.texte: The City lends three buildings free of charge to organizations for the winter: the church at 5600, 12e Avenue to the Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal, the former monastery of the Recluses Missionnaires at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est to Projets Autochtones du Québec, and the Bain St-Denis at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert to L'Amour en Action SYL DAN. The loans end on April 30, 2026 and the value of the unbilled rent is estimated at $57,076 for the church.

Verdun pays $12,950 to Société de développement social to keep outreach workers in its municipal facilities from January 5 to February 6, 2026. Ahuntsic-Cartierville ratifies the continuation of the contract with Les services de cohabitation sociale COHAB inc. for a warming centre for the winter of 2025-2026.

The City grants financial support to community organizations under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs 2026-2028, for projects on inclusion, cohabitation in public space and awareness. The amounts cover a three-year period ending December 31, 2028.

etapes.titre: Private donations and fitting-out of the Bain St-Denis
etapes.texte: Council adopts a framework to receive private donations intended for housing, shelter and social cohabitation projects; donors do not choose the project funded. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie transfers $250,000 for the activities and fitting-out work of the temporary warming centre at the Bain Saint-Denis. City council also adopts a declaration of support for people experiencing homelessness and a motion on a rent support fund.

etapes.titre: Encampments on rue Notre-Dame and appeal proceedings
etapes.texte: The City awards a contract of $149,520, taxes included, to Mission Old Brewery to guide people from the rue Notre-Dame encampment sector toward shelter and housing, and pays $90,000 to the Réseau d'aide aux personnes seules et itinérantes de Montréal for the 2026, 2027 and 2028 editions of the Nuit des sans-abri. The executive committee takes charge of the dispute over the encampments under the Van Horne viaduct and authorizes an appeal of the ruling of June 8, 2026.

aSurveiller.texte: Mission Old Brewery's mandate in the rue Notre-Dame encampment sector ends on October 18, 2026.
The agreement between Ville-Marie and Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles for the public works team runs until May 15, 2027.
Support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs ends on December 31, 2028.

logement.description: Subsidies, land and social, affordable or student housing projects, including those of the SHDM and the OMHM.
logement.enBref: This year, the City approves the 2026 budgets of the SHDM and the OMHM, transfers or purchases land for social housing, and grants subsidies to organizations building affordable housing. It also amends the by-law that requires developers to include social and affordable housing in their projects.

etapes.texte: City council approves the 2026 budget of the Société d'habitation et de développement de Montréal, which manages 393 buildings and more than 5,200 affordable housing units [CM26 0114]. City council and the urban agglomeration council approve the 2026 budget of the Office municipal d'habitation de Montréal, which houses 42,587 households [CG26 0024].

The City accepts from the Government of Canada half the rights to a 3,658.8 square-metre plot of land on rue Jolicoeur, in Pierrefonds-Roxboro, at no cost [CG26 0042]. It also transfers, at no cost, to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni a 789.6 square-metre plot of land at 7965, boulevard de l'Acadie, where the cooperative must build 26 housing units [CG26 0062].

The City adds $877,312 to its assistance to Mission Unitaînés for a 100-unit building for seniors in Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve [CG26 0171]. It grants $581,845 to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni for the Acadie project [CG26 0178].

etapes.titre: Land purchase and right of first refusal
etapes.texte: The City purchases, for $9,293,113 plus taxes, a vacant 1,535.1 square-metre plot of land near rues Chatham and William, in the Sud-Ouest, for social housing purposes [CG26 0286]. It removes the right of first refusal for social housing on lots in Ville-Marie and Sud-Ouest that have been subject to it since 2020 [CG26 0292].

The City pays $25,110,800 to the Société du Patrimoine Angus Résidentiel for 350 affordable housing units at the Technopôle Angus [CG26 0372] and $13,151,528 to Immobilier collectif – Point commun for 395 housing units in Pointe-Saint-Charles [CG26 0559]. The executive committee authorizes the SHDM to build 72 housing units on 2e Avenue [CE26 1028], and Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopts a policy to reimburse 50% of permit fees for eligible projects [CA26 170209].

aSurveiller.texte: Occupancy of the 350 housing units at the Technopôle Angus no later than April 30, 2027.
Delivery of the SHDM's 72-unit building on 2e Avenue in May 2028.
Occupancy of the 395-unit building in Pointe-Saint-Charles in February 2030.
Integration of the fee exemption into the 2027 local fee schedule by-law in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood built on municipal land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, transitional developments.

etapes.texte: City council extended the lease of a 2,787 square-metre site to the Société de transport de Montréal, south of rue de Louvain and west of boulevard Saint-Laurent, for a total rent of $49,293. It also extended the lease of a neighbouring 836 square-metre site to an app-based parking company, for $45,049 before taxes.

City council named the new street at the heart of the eco-district "avenue des Solidarités," because the first residential project is under construction and addresses need to be assigned. The name came from a public call for proposals held in fall 2024.

etapes.titre: Contract for the street and the soil
etapes.texte: The City awarded Charex inc. the construction of a 610-metre street with sewer, water supply, lighting and underground electrical network, for $10,311,940.25 including taxes, with a total expenditure of $15,366,336. The contract includes the remediation of the soil of the former gas station, for which the City is adding $2,007,312.15 net through the environmental liability reserve.

The borough adopted a draft resolution authorizing the demolition of a building on avenue de l'Esplanade and the construction of a set of buildings, with a minimum density of 200 dwellings per hectare. It then launched a draft by-law allowing, on part of the municipal site at 50 and 150, rue de Louvain Ouest, a height limit of 73 metres and a floor area ratio of 6.

etapes.titre: Redevelopment of rue de Louvain Est
etapes.texte: The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension awarded Groupe MPotvin the redevelopment of rue de Louvain between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum of $8,199,514.82 including taxes and a total expenditure of $11,192,464.62. In October, it authorized the filing of an application for financial assistance to the ministère des Transports for the bike lane and sidewalks of this section.

aSurveiller.texte: The lease of the Laboratoire sur l'agriculture urbaine runs from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027; the Ville en vert vegetable garden is loaned until December 31, 2027.
Îlot 84 could occupy the Esplanade site from April 1 to October 31, 2027.
Work on rue de Louvain continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks and curbs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).
Four other public spaces in the eco-district remain to be named before the completion of developments, expected around 2032.

matieres-residuelles.description: Collections, sorting centres, biomethanization and ecocentres.
matieres-residuelles.enBref: This year, the City is changing the days, sectors and frequency of collections in several boroughs, and buying bins for residents. It is extending its food waste treatment contracts and its contracts related to ecocentres, and awarding a contract to process mattresses. It is also tabling the agglomeration's 2025 residual materials management report.

etapes.texte: The City extends twice, by six months each time, its contracts with Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. to compost or biomethanize food waste from the eastern part of the agglomeration. The materials are transferred in Montréal-Est and then treated in Saint-Thomas-de-Joliette and in Moose Creek, Ontario, while waiting for the Montréal-Est organic materials treatment centre to come into service.

etapes.titre: Bin purchase and sorting equipment loans
etapes.texte: City council concludes agreements with Orbis Canada and USD Global to supply collection bins to residents of the boroughs, then with Plasti-Bac inc. for garbage bins for Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension. The executive committee approves an agreement with Tricentris, which pays $43,773.61, taxes included, for a program to lend reusable dishware, water fountains and sorting stations for neighbourhood events.

etapes.titre: Containers, ecocentres and former dump sites
etapes.texte: The agglomeration extends the contracts for garbage collection from front-loading and semi-underground containers, as well as the container contract for the écocentre Saint-Laurent. It awards Recyc-Matelas inc. a contract worth $734,690.25, taxes included, to collect and process mattresses and box springs from ecocentres, assigns two firms to carry out studies on buildings located on former waste disposal sites, and extends the contract for the software that manages discharge authorizations.

aSurveiller.texte: The program to lend dishware, water fountains and sorting stations is offered until no later than December 31, 2026.
The extension of the food waste treatment contracts runs until February 28, 2027.
The écocentre Saint-Laurent container contract and the container collection contracts are extended until October 31, 2027.
The contract for the discharge authorization management software covers the period from October 12, 2026 to October 11, 2029.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack: sale of land, loan by-laws, waterworks for the Namur–De la Savane sector.
namur-hippodrome.enBref: The City is preparing the future neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. It obtained an extended deadline from Québec to sell a first piece of land, adopted two loan by-laws for waterworks and public domain works, and transferred a piece of land to an organization for non-market housing. At the same time, it is leasing parcels of the site to organizations for temporary uses.

etapes.titre: Deadline postponed to sell a first piece of land
etapes.texte: The Québec government grants the City a deadline until October 31, 2027 to sell a first piece of land on the site of the former racetrack, west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. The postponement does not involve any financial compensation, and the other conditions of the 2017 deed of transfer remain the same.

City council approves a City guarantee of $2,000,000 in favour of the Canada Infrastructure Bank, for a loan to Société GALOPH that is used to pay for feasibility studies for the residential project. The same day, council rejects a motion from the Official Opposition on governance and the management of assets and public funds in the development of the neighbourhood.

The City borrows $29,000,000 to develop the public domain of the neighbourhood: soil remediation, sewers and waterworks, street redevelopment, fees and land purchases. It also borrows $12,000,000 to build water mains between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.

etapes.titre: Four buildings authorized on rue Namur
etapes.texte: The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopts a draft resolution authorizing the construction of four residential buildings in four phases, at 7301 boulevard Décarie and 5150-5160 rue Namur. One of the buildings must house a municipal sports and leisure centre, and the developer must pay $3,200,000 for public amenities and equipment in the sector.

The City leases parcels of the site to the community cafeteria MultiCaf and to Coopérative de solidarité Polliflora for temporary urban agriculture, as well as to Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for a transitional nursery. Each lease provides for a token rent, and the organizations pay for development, maintenance and property taxes.

aSurveiller.texte: Deadline granted by the Québec government to sell a first piece of land on the site: October 31, 2027.
The federal grant of $128.3M is conditional on the infrastructure being completed by 2031; the funds from the $29,000,000 loan cover work from 2026 to 2028.
Communia has five years after the signing of the deed of transfer to complete at least one building, and housing affordability must last at least 25 years.
End of temporary leases: April 30, 2027 for MultiCaf, March 31, 2028 for Polliflora, and April 30, 2028 for the transitional nursery.

parcs.description: Development and renovation of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.

etapes.titre: Plans and studies before the work
etapes.texte: The City is giving the winning team of an architecture competition the job of designing the bibliothèque Caroline-Dawson and redeveloping parc Le Prévost, for a total expense of $10,559,257.81, taxes included. It is also paying $174,471.56 to Verdun for soil and environmental studies at parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard, which was built on a former dump.

The City is adding $162,897.98 to the contract for repairing the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, having a culvert rebuilt at the pôle agricole du Bois-de-la-Roche, and awarding contracts for snow removal and the felling of ash trees and dying trees. It is listing the Anse-à-l'Orme area in the directory of protected natural environments and filing Cap-Saint-Jacques's candidacy for the Urban Night Sky Place designation.

The City and the boroughs are adding amounts or shifting budgets for work already underway: oversight of parc du Bassin-à-Bois, parcs des Hirondelles and du Sault-au-Récollet, parc Villeray, plans for parc Percy-Walters, and the museum exhibit design for the parc des Sœurs de Sainte-Anne in Lachine.

City council is removing an 810.2 m² stretch of street from the public domain to add it to parc Campbell Ouest, in Sud-Ouest. Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is requesting the same thing for a 75.2 m² strip of laneway that runs through parc Le Prévost.

aSurveiller.texte: City council must rule on October 19, 2026 on the removal of the laneway strip from parc Le Prévost, after it goes before the executive committee on October 7, 2026.
For the artwork at parc des Eaux-Cachées: the winner will be chosen in October 2026, the contract awarded in December 2026, and installation will happen in 2028.
The snow removal contract for the Grand parc de l'Ouest covers the period from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
Final acceptance of the work at parc du Bassin-à-Bois is expected in June 2027, after the one-year warranty period.

For the Cap-Saint-Jacques candidacy: the lighting plan will be filed in February 2027, a response from DarkSky International is expected in April 2027, and the site will be brought into compliance in April 2032.
Work at parc J.O.R.-Leduc, in LaSalle, is expected to be completed in June 2028.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and commercial activity ordinances.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City is funding and regulating temporary pedestrian streets on commercial thoroughfares, mainly for the 2026 summer season. The executive committee paid $2,694,500 to boroughs under the call for projects for pedestrianization on commercial thoroughfares [CE26 0465], and the boroughs adopted the ordinances that close the streets, authorize terraces, sales and music. Other decisions concern public squares: development, change of status of a lot and official name.

etapes.titre: Subsidy rules and settlement of a dispute
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law allowing it to subsidize its commercial development corporations for pedestrianizing streets, up to $425 per linear metre, provided council closes the street by ordinance [CA26 240037]. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie settles out of court for $41,686.46 a lawsuit related to work on the public square at the corner of rue Beaubien Est and rue Boyer [CA26 26 0010].

The executive committee distributes $2,694,500 among boroughs for pedestrian streets closed for at least eight consecutive weeks, including rue Villeray as a new project [CE26 0465]. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce creates the Placette CDN from April 1 to October 31, 2026 [CA26 170058] and Ville-Marie bans traffic on the sections of its summer pedestrianizations [CA26 240090].

The boroughs pay contributions to the commercial development corporations that organize the pedestrian streets: $102,045 for rue Villeray [CA26 14 0078], $375,500 for rue Sainte-Catherine Est [CA26 240134] and $67,500 for avenue Lacombe until 2028 [CA26 170108]. Outremont allocates $105,000 to the pedestrianization of avenue Bernard, in addition to a $106,000 grant from the Service du développement économique [CA26 16 0061].

The borough councils close their thoroughfares to cars and regulate terraces, sales and noise: avenue Bernard from May 19 to September 24 [CA26 16 0082], avenues Royal and Madison from June 1 to October 31 [CA26 170088], rue Ontario Est from June 15 to September 18 [CA26 27 0115], avenues du Mont-Royal and Duluth [CA26 25 0134]. Ville-Marie adjusts the dates of three pedestrianizations [CA26 240155] and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve removes 113 paid parking spaces [CA26 27 0119].

etapes.titre: Public squares and end of season
etapes.texte: City council changes the status of a 899-square-metre lot at the corner of rue Sherbrooke Est and boulevard Langelier from street (public square) to local park [CM26 0888] and names the public square at the corner of rue Charleroi and avenue L'Archevêque « place Chez-Marguerite » [CM26 0913]. Ville-Marie authorizes the sound ambiance on the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles [CA26 240372] and Le Plateau-Mont-Royal revises the reopening schedule for avenue du Mont-Royal [CA26 25 227].

aSurveiller.texte: Avenue du Mont-Royal reopens to traffic between Saint-Denis and Resther on September 30, 2026, and between Saint-Laurent and Saint-Denis on October 15, 2026.
The boroughs must report on the amounts received for pedestrianizations in November 2026 and return any unspent money in December 2026.
The ordinance on the sound ambiance of the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles runs until September 2, 2027.
The on-demand transit contract on avenue du Mont-Royal covers until December 31, 2027, and support for the pedestrianization of avenue Lacombe until December 31, 2028.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.titre: Requests for extension to the ministry
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville is requesting twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is requesting six additional months, after a first extension obtained in July 2025.

Following the public consultation of March 25, 2026, Ville-Marie is reviewing its rules on urban planning, special projects, demolition, certificates and cadastral operations. The by-law authorizes a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and allows public transit stations in category E.1 sectors.

The borough is changing heights, uses and the building coverage ratio in the sector bordered by avenue Papineau, avenue Émile-Journault, avenue André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est, and is increasing the permitted heights on sections of rue Lajeunesse. It is also amending its by-law on the demolition of buildings, following a public meeting held on June 23, 2026.

aSurveiller.texte: Saint-Laurent's public consultation on its three draft by-laws, on October 20, 2026 at 7 p.m.
Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce: public consultation on October 21, 2026 and adoption on November 2, 2026; the deadline granted by the minister runs until December 16, 2026.
Saint-Léonard must adopt all its concordance by-laws by June 16, 2027, a date set by the Minister of Municipal Affairs.
Ahuntsic-Cartierville is requesting an extension until June 16, 2027.
Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension has until June 17, 2027 to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.
L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève plans to present its project to elected officials starting mid-June 2026 and to hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.

securite-publique.description: The City of Montréal Police Service (SPVM): contracts, neighbourhood stations, council motions.

etapes.titre: Loan for equipment and loan of a police officer
etapes.texte: City council adopts a by-law authorizing a loan of $10,880,000 to purchase and replace specialized public safety equipment for the SPVM between 2026 and 2030. It also authorizes the loan of a detective sergeant to the RCMP team that enforces the Firearms Act, starting January 7, 2026.

The City awards 9415-1966 Québec inc. the contract for meals for people detained by the SPVM and extends by one year the software maintenance for the computer-aided dispatch system with Peraton International. It leases 50 parking spaces from the Société de la Place des arts, extends the lease of the training centre in Anjou and that of neighbourhood station 15 in Verdun, and accepts $8,000 from Ottawa for a sexual assault awareness campaign.

etapes.titre: Ammunition, courier services and building trades
etapes.texte: The City enters into an agreement with Agence Gravel for 9 mm practice ammunition for firearms training, extends the SPVM's courier contract by one year, and renews the lease for neighbourhood station 26 on avenue Mountain Sights. It also selects suppliers for carpentry and painting services in SPVM buildings, and loans a detective sergeant to the Sûreté du Québec team on the exportation of stolen vehicles.

aSurveiller.texte: October 23, 2026: "Fèves au lard" day organized by the Fraternité des policiers et policières at neighbourhood station 46, for which the Anjou borough purchased 62 tickets.
February 1, 2027: start of the 10-year lease for the metro unit premises of neighbourhood station 50, at 888 boulevard De Maisonneuve Est.
March 1, 2027: deadline for delivery of the port patrol boat and its trailer.
March 31, 2027: end of the period covered by the grants from the ACCES Tabac, ACCES Alcool, ACCES Cannabis and ACCEF committees.

velo.titre: Bike: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and bike lanes, and the self-service bike BIXI.
velo.enBref: This year, the City mainly bought equipment for the BIXI self-service bike system, paid for work on existing bike lanes, and settled the occupation of Hydro-Québec land crossed by bike paths. Boroughs awarded maintenance and development contracts, and the City asked Québec for money for four new bike construction projects.

etapes.texte: Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie passed an order that formalizes the bike lanes on avenue Christophe-Colomb between rues des Carrières and de Bellechasse and imposes mandatory manoeuvres on drivers up to Jean-Talon Est. Outremont authorized $100,000 for de-icing salt and abrasives spread notably on its bike paths.

etapes.titre: Bike path repairs and sustainable mobility corridors
etapes.texte: City council added $3,400,000 to the contract with Bruneau Électrique inc. for sustainable mobility corridors in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, then approved Ville-Marie and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension carrying out road surface and bike lane work, including the repair of the REV Lajeunesse between Jarry and Crémazie. Ahuntsic-Cartierville retained Déneigement et Excavation M. Gauthier inc. for the spring cleaning of narrow paths.

City council awarded a sole-source contract of $4,815,802.61 to PBSC Solutions Urbaines inc. for bikes, stations and docking points compatible with the BIXI system. The executive committee then retained Laser AMP, a division of ISE Métal inc., for $394,851.17, to supply the steel pavers that serve as the base for stations.

Outremont tabled a draft by-law to convert the shared lane on avenue Lajoie, between Stuart and Outremont, into a one-way bike path. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal awarded Cojalac inc. work on rue Parthenais including a BIXI station, and the Sud-Ouest awarded Groupe Damex inc. the development of three green alleys and the electrical installation of a BIXI station.

etapes.titre: Requests for financial assistance from Québec
etapes.texte: City council authorized the filing of four requests for financial assistance to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable, for bike lanes and sidewalks on rues de Champlain, Saint-Jacques, Guy and Laurier. The City commits to paying at least half of the eligible expenses.

aSurveiller.texte: October 9, 2026: deadline to file complete financial assistance requests with the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable.
The repair of the bike lane on rue De Louvain, between west of rue d'Iberville and boulevard Saint-Michel, is budgeted at $570,000 in 2027.
